newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds down in cautious trade, focus on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds down in cautious trade, focus on U.S..

text.p: Irish bonds were down in cautious late trade on Monday in line with overseas markets ahead of the testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to Congress, dealers said.
Greenspan is scheduled to deliver his semi-annual Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Tuesday and Wednesday and dealers said his comments would be crucial for the dollar.

"The Irish market is primarily down because international markets are down," one dealer said. "International markets are nervous ahead of what Greenspan might say in his testimony and how it might affect the dollar."

By 1615 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 dropped 22 pence from Friday's close to 103.00 to yield 5.73 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had eased 25 pence from the close at 111.05 to yield 6.40 percent.

Dealers said while Monday's auction of 150 million Irish pounds of the variable rate bond due 2000 by Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) had been covered 4.12 times, the auction had little impact on trade.
"It was only a floatation rate, nothing to get too excited about," one dealer said.
Domestic focus will turn to the release of Ireland's monthly consumer price data for January on Tuesday.
The Central Statistics Office (CSO) previously published the consumer price index (CPI) on a quarterly basis but is moving to monthly releases as part of an EU data harmonisation process.

"It will be hard to compare Tuesday's data with anything that has gone before because of the move away from quarterly releases. It will be two to three months before any kind of comparisons can be done." one dealer said.
"But it is likely to be a good number," he added.
The forecast is for an increase of 0.1 or 0.3 percent on the fourth quarter of 1996 while the index is expected to rise by 1.7 to 1.8 percent on the first quarter of last year
